description:
Building Operational Technology Integration Specialist  (Senior or Lead)

Company:
The Boeing Company

Boeing’s Enterprise Services Technology & Systems (ESTS) organization is currently seeking a Building Operational Technology Integration Specialist  (Senior or Lead) to join our Building Operational Technology team. This is primarily a remote position, with domestic travel to our site locations required up to 25% of the time, including but not limited to Arlington VA, Huntsville AL, Mesa AZ, North Charleston SC, Plano TX, Renton WA, Puget Sound WA, or Wichita KS. Our team is open to a broad range of experience levels including Level 4 and Level 5 Specialists to find the best fit for the position.

This position requires someone who thrives in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. You will be a key contributor to building and advancing the Operational Technology (OT) team, responsible for integrating systems, platforms, and data that support critical industrial and infrastructure systems. You will fulfill a broad range of responsibilities that are expected to change and evolve often as the Operational Technology landscape continues to develop. The ability to adapt and innovate within complex operational environments is paramount to being successful in this role.

Position Responsibilities:

- Build processes, standards, and operational frameworks from the ground up

- Assesses current Operational Technology systems for compliance with IT and OT cybersecurity standards and regulations

- Support technical troubleshooting and remediation for Building Management Systems / Building Automation Systems, including controllers, field devices, sensors, and system integrations

- Analyze and resolve Building Management System alarms, faults, and abnormal conditions; determine root cause (software, hardware, instrumentation, network) and implement corrective actions to reduce nuisance alarms and false trips

- Support alarm rationalization and tuning of fault detection and diagnostics (FDD) rules, applying the enterprise alarm and fault priority standard to improve signal quality and reduce operator workload

- Evaluate integrations between Building Management Systems and enterprise systems (Information Technology interfaces, fault management, analytic platforms, and Computerized Maintenance Management System) to ensure reliable data flow and operational visibility

- Support nationwide rollout and integration of the enterprise Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) platform for building and infrastructure monitoring; analyze configuration and connectivity issues and coordinate fixes with the site teams, integrators, and vendors

- Facilitate discussions and meetings to address IT compliance requirements and operational needs, to include forecasting of new systems or enhancements and upgrades of existing systems

- Troubleshoot industrial communication networks and protocols (BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, Ethernet/IP) including use of network analyzers and diagnostic tools

- Assist with the development and maintenance of technical documentation, including integration specifications, as-built configurations, and site onboarding records

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):

- Bachelor’s degree or higher

- 5+ years of experience with Operational Technology

- 5+ years of experience in Real Estate, Facilities Operations and/or Facilities Management

- Experience collecting, organizing, synthesizing, and analyzing data, then summarizing findings; developing conclusions and recommendations from appropriate data sources

- Experience developing and managing internal processes and procedures
- Domestic travel up to 25%

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):

- 10+ years' related work experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience
- Experience with Operational Technology, industrial control systems, and relevant IT and OT frameworks (e.g., NIST SP 800-82, ISA/IEC 62443, ISO 27001)

- Experience in facilities Operational Technology (OT) systems, industrial control systems or facilities maintenance systems

- Experience with SCADA and HMI platforms such as ICONICS GENESIS64, Niagara Framework, or COPA-DATA zenon

- Experience with major Building Automation System vendor platforms (e.g., Johnson Controls Metasys, Siemens Desigo, Honeywell, Schneider Electric EcoStruxure)

- Experience with fault detection and diagnostics (FDD), alarm management (e.g., ANSI/ISA-18.2), or building analytics platforms

- Experience with cybersecurity principles specific to OT environments, including risk assessment and mitigation strategies

- Experience with multi-site programs and demonstrated ability to lead initiatives across geographic locations

- Experience with project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Scrum, Waterfall) and project management tools (e.g., Wrike, Microsoft Project, Jira)

The team: The Software Engineering and Systems Integration team in the UK is actively working across Boeing Defence, Commercial Airplanes, Global services and Uncrewed technologies.

The Software Engineering team works in the development of Synthetic Environment Sub-systems, Mission Systems Capability, Autonomous Behaviours, enhancement of Ground Control Systems, Technical Publications and various in-house proprietary tools for the Defence platforms. The team is also contributing to Commercial Modification of aircrafts, development of Onboard Network Systems, Cabin Interiors and supporting Supplemental Type Certification effort.

About the role

You’ll support Defence and Security domains at Boeing locations and Customer sites across the UK, including Autonomous Systems, Training and Simulation, Cyber, Space, Intelligence and Security.

You will join a rapidly growing Engineering Capability with a culture for development, collaboration and success. Initially you will be assigned to our Simulation Programmes, which operate across the Air, Land and Maritime domains, with future opportunity to develop your interests across the breadth of the Software Engineering portfolio.

- Supports designing, modeling, simulation, testing, and analysis to assess and optimize overall system performance and capabilities.

title: Little Mountain Test Facility Senior Program Manager & Site Manager
description:
Little Mountain Test Facility Senior Program Manager & Site Manager

Company:
The Boeing Company

Boeing is seeking a highly experienced Senior Program Manager & Site Manager to lead the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Little Mountain Test Facility (LMTF) Operations & Maintenance (O&M) Program, located in Ogden, Utah, at a Hill Air Force Base (HAFB) annex.

The Boeing Senior Program Manager & Site Manager serves as the senior leader responsible for the overall execution, performance, and administration of Boeing’s Strategic Deterrence Systems (SDS) program at LMTF. This position provides on-site leadership for day-to-day execution and holds primary responsibility, accountability, and authority for LMTF’s O&M program, including associated delivery order CLINs for add-on test contracts, equipment purchase contracts, new test capability contracts, facility support contracts, and all commercial test execution contracts performed under the LMTF Cooperative Research & Development Agreement (CRADA).

This role also provides leadership oversight for LMTF modernization and future growth initiatives, including research, development, design, and integration of new technology insertions supporting nuclear hardness test capabilities and facility development. In addition, the Program Manager & Site Manager is responsible for overseeing site operations, serving as the primary Boeing interface and point of contact to Government stakeholders, maintaining a safe and compliant work environment, and ensuring LMTF laboratories and facilities remain fully operational and effective in support of mission requirements.

The Program Manager & Site Manager is the key operational leader for LMTF’s complex and unique test laboratories, sustainment activities, and safety-sensitive environments involving functional interfaces across multiple laboratories and facilities, maintenance coordination, and mission-critical test schedule execution. This position directs operational, technical, staffing, safety, security, cyber, quality, and sustainment activities necessary to support mission-critical testing, maintenance, facility operations, and modernization efforts in accordance with contractual requirements and Government direction. Other responsibilities include developing and maintaining an overall program organizational structure aligned with contractual cost and execution requirements, mission priorities, and overall program objectives. This includes ensuring appropriate personnel are assigned to each position with the applicable skills, experience, and staffing levels to effectively support program execution while remaining within overall program cost constraints.

The Boeing Program Manager & Site Manager is responsible for ensuring contract compliance, mission readiness, and successful delivery of all program objectives through leadership of a team of 100+ employees and support staff, including lab and engineering managers, site operations managers, engineers, scientists, technicians, program and project specialists, business operations staff, and support personnel. This position includes direct oversight of project specialists, business operations staff, and first-line managers supporting LMTF’s program management, business operations, and site support functions.

LMTF supports the AFNWC mission by providing test environments to study, analyze, and evaluate the effects of nuclear and operational conditions on ICBM weapon systems in support of warfighter nuclear capabilities. The mission directly supports the AFNWC ICBM portfolio, including Minuteman III and Sentinel. LMTF’s primary focus is to support Minuteman III and Sentinel weapon system testing, as well as other AFNWC portfolio programs, Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of Energy (DOE) programs, and approved mission partners requiring testing to assess system survivability, vulnerability, and performance. LMTF’s vision is to ensure its test capabilities and facilities meet sustainment, modernization, and mission requirements, safeguarding the land-based leg of the nuclear triad and providing test support to other mission partners as available.

Primary (Core) Responsibilities

Boeing’s Program Manager & Site Manager is responsible for leading and directing all phases of the LMTF program. The primary core responsibilities include:

- Program Execution:
- Lead program planning, execution, financial management, and stakeholder reporting for the LMTF portfolio, including sustainment, testing, and modernization efforts.
- Ensure program objectives are achieved in alignment with contractual commitments, technical requirements, and customer expectations.

- Cost Management & Resource Allocation:
- Serve as the primary Cost Account Manager (CAM) with direct oversight of budgets, resources, and schedules.
- Ensure appropriate staffing levels and resource allocations are established across all functional areas.
- Coordinate new or redirected resources across all site functions as required.
- Oversee technical management of suppliers and drive process improvements.
- Coordinate emergency response, after-hours response, and urgent operational needs as required.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to obtain support for specialized nuclear hardness requirements.
- Partner with cross-functional teams to address specialized requests and on-site support to meet mission requirements (e.g. Supplier Management, Corporate “P-Card Compliance”, Quality, Safety, Logistics, etc.).

- Program Status & Performance:
- Track and report program status and performance, including cost, schedule, technical performance, operational status, and mission impacts, to program leadership and Government representatives.
- Participate in and/or lead internal and external program management reviews, technical interchange meetings, readiness reviews, customer briefings, and site tours and visits from Distinguished Visitors (DVs).
- Establish and maintain weekly and monthly reviews and status calls with key Government stakeholders.
- Lead daily Tier meetings, weekly staff meetings, and monthly all employee meetings.
- Develop, implement, and maintain a site Risk, Issue, and Opportunity (RIO) management plan.

- Program Compliance:
- Maintain compliance with customer, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
- Maintain adherence to applicable security, radiation safety, cybersecurity, environmental, health, safety, and other functional requirements as applicable.
- Oversee and verify that all contractual deliverables are completed accurately and delivered on schedule.

- Overall Program Leadership:
- Serve as the primary site-level point of contact for all Government stakeholders.
- Coordinate daily program execution across all functional support activities, including nuclear hardness and survivability laboratories, test stands, facilities, maintenance, logistics, and support teams.

- Modernization & Program Growth:
- Support and drive new business opportunities and growth across LMTF’s modernization of facilities, laboratories, and nuclear hardness test capabilities.
- Lead future program opportunities and proposal efforts supporting long-term sustainment and growth.

- Personnel Management & Mentorship:
- Manage direct reports, including schedules, performance reviews, and ongoing workforce coordination.
- Provide mentorship, guidance, and professional development for site programs, project, and business operations staff.
- Foster collaboration between the program office and site teams.

- Safety & Quality:
- Champion and promote a strong site-wide culture of safety, quality, compliance, and continuous improvement.
- Communicate the importance of safety and ensure all personnel understand safety as a top priority.
- Drive continuous improvement and quality-focused practices across all LMTF functions.
